Chapter 1: Chapter 1 — The Artemis Accord

6|
7|

![](chapter_images/ch01.png)

8|

The transmission from Houston arrived at 03:14 UTC, seven minutes before the vote, and Tom Chen knew before he opened it that his life was about to end.

9|

Chen — the Chinese delegation has withdrawn its support. The treaty will fail without a unanimous Security Council. Your father is requesting you call him before the vote.

10|

He read the message standing in the comms alcove of the Orion transfer vehicle, one hand braced against the bulkhead, the recycled air suddenly thin in his lungs. Eighty-three days of negotiations.

11|

And now this.

12|

His father wanted him to call. Which meant his father wanted him to listen. To the arguments about sovereignty.

13|

Tom Chen closed the message and looked at the clock. Six minutes until the Security Council vote. Five minutes, forty-seven seconds to decide whether to defy his father, his country, and every expectation that had been placed on him since he was old enough to hold a welding torch.

14|

The bridge had been the first time.

15|

Ellis, you son of a bitch. You should have listened to me.

16|

He squeezed his eyes shut and the memory came back in high-definition color, the way trauma always did. The Kanawha River Bridge, West Virginia, October 12th, 2029. He was twenty-nine years old, the youngest structural engineer on the project, and he'd flagged the stress-fracture readings in the Number 4 pier three weeks before the collapse. Written the report.

17|

The bridge had collapsed during evening rush hour. Thirty-seven vehicles. Sixty-two dead. Ellis had been the safety inspector who'd signed off on the pier inspection two days before the collapse — signed off because the project lead assured him the microfractures were within tolerance.

18|

Tom had testified. He'd told the inquiry exactly what he'd seen, exactly when he'd seen it, exactly who he'd told. The project lead went to prison. The engineering firm collapsed. Tom Chen became the whistleblower who'd tried to save the bridge, and the man who couldn't save his friend.

19|

He was thirty now. Thirty-one in two months. And the Moon was offering him a second chance.

20|

He keyed the comm. "Houston, this is Chen. I am not calling my father. Put me through to the Security Council chamber."

21|

"Chen, the Chinese delegation specifically requested—"

22|

"Put me through."

23|

The hesitation lasted three seconds. Then the channel opened.

24|

The Security Council chamber materialized on his display — a horseshoe of delegations, translators murmuring into headsets, the Secretary-General at the podium. The Chinese ambassador, Wei Zhang, was on his feet, speaking in rapid Mandarin without waiting for translation.

25|

Tom muted his feed, took a breath, and considered his options.

26|

The Artemis Accord was not a perfect document. It was a compromise — a thousand compromises, stitched together by exhausted negotiators who'd spent two years arguing over paragraphs. It gave the Moon to no nation and all nations.

27|

It was also the only thing standing between humanity's first permanent off-world settlement and the chaos of national competition that had already started. China was building a lander. The US already had Orion.

28|

Without the Accord, the Moon would become a battlefield. With it — flawed, fragile, infuriatingly political — there was at least a framework.

29|

Tom unmuted his feed. "Ambassador Zhang, this is Tom Chen, attached to the US delegation as mission structural engineer. May I speak?"

30|

Wei Zhang's face tightened. He knew exactly who Tom Chen was. Son of Minister Chen Liwei. Grandson of General Chen Xueliang. A Chen, speaking against China in the Security Council.

31|

"You may speak, Engineer Chen. But choose your words carefully."

32|

Tom stood up in the zero-G of the Orion cabin, letting the restraint harness catch his weight. His heart was hammering. His palms were slick. But his voice was steady.

33|

"The treaty does not guarantee—"

34|

The chamber was silent. Tom could see the Secretary-General staring at him with an expression that was half gratitude, half horror.

35|

The silence stretched.

36|

Ambassador Zhang stared at his display for a long moment. Then he sat down, exchanged a whispered consultation with his deputy, and raised his hand.

37|

"China withdraws its objection. We will vote in favor."

38|

The vote passed 15-0.

39|

Tom collapsed into the seat, the restraint harness catching him, and listened to the Secretary-General's formal announcement through a roaring in his ears. The Artemis Accord was law. The first permanent lunar settlement was authorized. Construction would begin within eighteen months.

40|

His comm chimed. A private channel. His father's voice, cold and precise.

41|

"You have made a powerful enemy of the Minister of Science. He will not forget this."

42|

"I know."

43|

"Your mother is crying."

44|

"I know that too."

45|

"I hope the Moon is worth your family, Tom."

46|

The channel closed.

47|

Tom stared at the bulkhead for a long time, watching the indicator lights blink their meaningless patterns. The Moon. He'd been fighting for the Moon for three years — the engineering, the logistics, the politics of getting a permanent habitat off the ground. He'd told himself it was about the science.

48|

But sitting in the dark of the Orion transfer vehicle, listening to the hum of the life support systems that would keep him alive on a world with no atmosphere and no second chances, Tom Chen admitted the truth.

49|

He was running. From the bridge. From the ghost of Ellis Kowalski. From the articles that called him a hero and the letters from widows that called him a coward for not screaming louder.

50|

He pulled up the photo of Maya on his tablet. She was wearing a dinosaur costume, Halloween 2030, her face split by a gap-toothed grin. He'd been in Geneva. He'd watched the video three hours late, after the negotiations finally broke for dinner.

51|

"I'm going to the Moon, baby girl," he whispered. "And I'm going to build something so strong it'll never fall down."

52|

The orbit insertion burn for Shackleton Crater was scheduled for 06:00. Tom had two hours to sleep, two hours to dream of bridges and bones and the cold weight of a planet that had killed his best friend.

53|

He closed his eyes and waited for the burn that would carry him beyond the reach of everything he'd ever known.

54|

The Artemis Accord was signed.

55|

The Foundation was born.

56|

And Tom Chen had just burned every bridge he'd ever built.

function.name: patch
function.description:
Targeted find-and-replace edits in files. Use this instead of sed/awk in terminal. Uses fuzzy matching (9 strategies) so minor whitespace/indentation differences won't break it. Returns a unified diff. Auto-runs syntax checks after editing.

REPLACE MODE (mode='replace', default): find a unique string and replace it. REQUIRED PARAMETERS: mode, path, old_string, new_string.
PATCH MODE (mode='patch'): apply V4A multi-file patches for bulk changes. REQUIRED PARAMETERS: mode, patch.

mode.description: Edit mode. 'replace' (default): requires path + old_string + new_string. 'patch': requires patch content only.

path.description: REQUIRED when mode='replace'. File path to edit.

old_string.description: REQUIRED when mode='replace'. Exact text to find and replace. Must be unique in the file unless replace_all=true. Include surrounding context lines to ensure uniqueness.

new_string.description: REQUIRED when mode='replace'. Replacement text. Pass empty string '' to delete the matched text.

replace_all.description: Replace all occurrences instead of requiring a unique match (default: false)

patch.description:
REQUIRED when mode='patch'. V4A format patch content. Format:
*** Begin Patch
*** Update File: path/to/file
@@ context hint @@
 context line
-removed line
+added line
*** End Patch

cross_profile.description: Opt out of the cross-profile soft guard. Defaults to false. Set true ONLY after explicit user direction to edit another Hermes profile's skills/plugins/cron/memories.

action.description: Action to perform on background processes

session_id.description: Process session ID (from terminal background output). Required for all actions except 'list'.

data.description: Text to send to process stdin (for 'write' and 'submit' actions)

timeout.description: Max seconds to block for 'wait' action. Returns partial output on timeout.

Use offset and limit for large files. Reads exceeding ~100K characters are rejected; use offset and limit to read specific sections of large files. NOTE: Cannot read images or binary files — use vision_analyze for images.

path.description: Path to the file to read (absolute, relative, or ~/path)

Search file contents or find files by name. Use this instead of grep/rg/find/ls in terminal. Ripgrep-backed, faster than shell equivalents.

Content search (target='content'): Regex search inside files. Output modes: full matches with line numbers, file paths only, or match counts.

File search (target='files'): Find files by glob pattern (e.g., '*.py', '*config*'). Also use this instead of ls — results sorted by modification time.

pattern.description: Regex pattern for content search, or glob pattern (e.g., '*.py') for file search

path.description: Directory or file to search in (default: current working directory)

file_glob.description: Filter files by pattern in grep mode (e.g., '*.py' to only search Python files)

limit.description: Maximum number of results to return (default: 50)

offset.description: Skip first N results for pagination (default: 0)

output_mode.description: Output format for grep mode: 'content' shows matching lines with line numbers, 'files_only' lists file paths, 'count' shows match counts per file

function.name: terminal
function.description:
Execute shell commands on a Linux environment. Filesystem usually persists between calls.

Do NOT use cat/head/tail to read files — use read_file instead.
Do NOT use grep/rg/find to search — use search_files instead.
Do NOT use ls to list directories — use search_files(target='files') instead.
Do NOT use sed/awk to edit files — use patch instead.
Do NOT use echo/cat heredoc to create files — use write_file instead.
Reserve terminal for: builds, installs, git, processes, scripts, network, package managers, and anything that needs a shell.

Foreground (default): Commands return INSTANTLY when done, even if the timeout is high. Set timeout=300 for long builds/scripts — you'll still get the result in seconds if it's fast. Prefer foreground for short commands.
Background: Set background=true to get a session_id. Almost always pair with notify_on_complete=true — bg without notify runs SILENTLY and you have no way to learn it finished short of calling process(action='poll') yourself. Two legitimate uses:
  (1) Long-lived processes that never exit (servers, watchers, daemons) — silent is correct, there's no exit to notify on.
  (2) Long-running bounded tasks (tests, builds, deploys, CI pollers, batch jobs) — MUST set notify_on_complete=true. Without it you'll either forget to poll or sit blocked waiting for the user to surface the result.
For servers/watchers, do NOT use shell-level background wrappers (nohup/disown/setsid/trailing '&') in foreground mode. Use background=true so Hermes can track lifecycle and output.
After starting a server, verify readiness with a health check or log signal, then run tests in a separate terminal() call. Avoid blind sleep loops.
Use process(action="poll") for progress checks, process(action="wait") to block until done.
Working directory: Use 'workdir' for per-command cwd.
PTY mode: Set pty=true for interactive CLI tools (Codex, Claude Code, Python REPL).

Do NOT use vim/nano/interactive tools without pty=true — they hang without a pseudo-terminal. Pipe git output to cat if it might page.

command.description: The command to execute on the VM

background.description: Run the command in the background. Almost always pair with notify_on_complete=true — without it, the process runs silently and you'll have no way to learn it finished short of calling process(action='poll') yourself (easy to forget, leading to silent blindness on long jobs). Two legitimate patterns: (1) Long-lived processes that never exit (servers, watchers, daemons) — these stay silent because there's no exit to notify on. (2) Long-running bounded tasks (tests, builds, deploys, CI pollers, batch jobs) — these MUST set notify_on_complete=true. For short commands, prefer foreground with a generous timeout instead.

notify_on_complete.description: When true (and background=true), you'll be automatically notified exactly once when the process finishes. **This is the right choice for almost every long-running task** — tests, builds, deployments, multi-item batch jobs, anything that takes over a minute and has a defined end. USE ONLY for truly rare, one-shot mid-process signals on LONG-LIVED processes that will never exit on their own — e.g. ['Application startup complete'] on a server so you know when to hit its endpoint, or ['migration done'] on a daemon. DO NOT use for: (1) end-of-run markers like 'DONE'/'PASS' — use notify_on_complete instead; (2) error patterns like 'ERROR'/'Traceback' in loops or multi-item batch jobs — they fire on every iteration and you'll hit the strike limit fast; (3) anything you'd ever combine with notify_on_complete.
